member.name: T:Storeasy.Infrastructure.Services.SecurityStampStore
member.summary:
Redis-backed revocation stamp store with the database (User.SessionStamp) as the durable source of truth. Reads are served from Redis for a cheap per-request check; on a cache miss (or any Redis failure) it falls back to the database and repopulates the cache, so a Redis outage degrades to one extra database round trip rather than breaking authentication.
A rotation writes the new stamp through to Redis and must run after the caller's transaction has committed. The read-through repopulation only adds a missing entry (SET NX), so a reader that loaded the old stamp from the database just before a rotation can never put it back over the new one.
While Redis is disconnected the cache is skipped altogether: a command sent to a reconnecting multiplexer waits in its backlog until the timeout, which would hold every authenticated request for seconds.
member.para: A rotation also closes the user's live connections opened with the old stamp ().

member.summary:
The job: reads the apps and builds of one store connection and saves them.
App Store Connect: every app the key sees (/v1/apps); a new one is linked to the storeasy app whose other store record has the same bundle id, otherwise it gets its own storeasy app.
Google Play: no list API, so the records added by package name are read one by one (the edit probe proves the service account's access). A record Play refuses that was never confirmed is removed with its empty app.
Microsoft Store: not read here (permanent failure). Microsoft connections are synced by the job (), which reads their icons too.
Builds are upserted by the store's build id. Then the icon of every record is read () and written to its storeasy app when it changed; a failed icon read is logged and leaves the app's icon as it was. An App Store or Google Play icon always replaces the one the app has, so it wins over a Microsoft Store icon. All writes are set based or bulk; the loops only call the store. App Store records that arrive on this connection get the connection's App Store Connect webhooks: every endpoint registered through the API is registered again (a job, which upserts per app). App Store records with an experiment or custom product page that has not ended get a job, so their states follow App Store Connect.
